# QA, Regression And Local Test Workspace

Status: Draft

## Outcome And Confirmed Scope

Provide two separately and explicitly invoked skills and a separate workspace package in this repository. They share one canonical durable test-case/suite library per tested project:

- `manual-testing` is the QA workflow. It discovers implemented behavior, designs acceptance/exploratory cases from a selected planning packet or standalone request, runs them, maintains reusable case/suite definitions and recommends scenarios for permanent automation.
- `regression-testing` consumes that project's compatible library, plans a full or explicitly bounded regression, and schedules its cases across authorized local/remote environments with resource-aware sequential/parallel execution. Workflow orchestration is mandatory under MT-022, not a planning option.
- The local workspace tool owns case/suite management and revisions, frozen run scope, results/attachments, a simple human web UI, basic settings and agent-facing MCP capabilities. Humans and agents use the same canonical state. Reuse the ready-made open-source Allure Report viewer rather than implement another report renderer. The UI also works through an explicit standalone local launch without an active AI agent.

Here, manual testing means that the agent designs cases and interprets live evidence, not that it executes each action through a separate model turn: necessary browser/HTTP interactions are driven by temporary scripts/code through background jobs or equivalent native execution. Neither skill authors a persistent automated test suite or changes application code. The implementation executor decides whether to automate a proposal and creates permanent project tests under separate authority. Existing authorized automation may be used for mapped cases. The workspace tool is not a replacement test executor or CI orchestrator.

Confirmed depth: **Deep**. Active profiles: **core**, **ui**, **backend**, **data**, **operations**, **security**, **cross-surface**. Keep the two skills, common library and local UI/MCP/reporting outcome in this one specification. No separate Git repository is selected. The first version excludes separate Shared steps, Defects, TestOps-style CI Jobs and custom Dashboards. This does not remove native background jobs, case dependencies, source links or the required Allure result view.

Planning owns technical agreements, the physical storage/search design, exact tool/protocol realization and compatible upstream dependency/version selection. SQLite and the old planning drafts are not approved technical choices. This invocation defines behavior only: it does not create the package, profile/design artifacts, skills, servers, dependencies, installations, commits or releases.

## Supported Environments And Verification Boundary

Both skills retain the collection's Codex, Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness distributions, one authoritative template per skill, isolated host output and actual capability discovery under MT-013/MT-022. The new tool must implement runtime compatibility with **Linux, Windows and macOS** and UI compatibility with stable desktop **Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox and Safari**. It is local and single-user, including cooperating agent sessions under that user's authority; a shared network/team service and mobile UI are not this delivery.

**Development verification is limited to Linux and real Google Chrome.** Other supported platforms/browsers are implemented requirements but explicitly unverified in this cycle, not unsupported and not passed. Do not silently relabel Chromium-only evidence as Google Chrome or add mandatory native all-platform checks to finish this cycle. Record exact observed versions and limitations. A later discovered incompatibility on a supported platform remains a defect. MT-028 owns this distinction; it is not a waiver of required Linux/Chrome checks or native workflow semantics.

Tested applications and stands are a different component: their OS/runtime/browser and local/remote placement remain task-dependent. Establish actual target identity, authority and available execution/resource capabilities per run. Missing capability blocks affected execution; do not invent observed compatibility. MT-024 applies on every relevant execution/managed-stand host.

A URL-only target still needs no repository, Git, planning bundle or engineering-workflow MCP solely for standalone testing. It does need an explicitly identified owned library and compatible workspace capability for required durable case/run operations. This testing runtime is distinct from the conditional engineering-workflow MCP used for packet conformance; neither installs the other automatically. Unavailable required persistence prevents a complete saved-run claim; preserve safe independent observations under MT-002/MT-010/MT-015. Regression requires its compatible project library, not a prior QA conversation or a new specification for each historical case.

## Requirements

### MT-001: Explicit Manual-Testing Authority

**Behavior.** Both skills run only after an explicit invocation for a named target or bounded testing outcome. Default public names are `manual-testing` for QA and `regression-testing` for regression. Their primary activity is agent-designed criterion-based testing, executed under MT-015 through MT-017. Neither creates, changes or maintains persistent automated tests, application code, configuration, dependency manifests, lockfiles or generated project code. Persistent tests and product fixes belong to a separately authorized `incremental-implementation` invocation. Temporary execution code may automate selected scenarios without becoming a project test suite. Existing safe authorized automation may execute cases whose coverage is actually mapped; it does not prove unrelated UI/API behavior or unmapped library cases.

Temporary scripts/probes are allowed only in a verified temporary directory outside project source. Durable writes are limited to the project test library and run metadata under MT-018 through MT-025 and the separate report/sanitized evidence under MT-010. This grants no other project-write authority. Do not invoke implementation, review, another planning packet, installation, commit or publication automatically. Neither skill is a new implementation-completion or next-packet gate. QA owns canonical case/suite maintenance; regression consumes those definitions and records run observations without silently rewriting expectations.

**Acceptance.** For a request to verify an implemented form, the agent prepares cases, uses temporary execution code through an available background/equivalent runner, and reports the form's actual behavior rather than spending model turns on every action. A project before/after change inventory shows no test, source, configuration or dependency edits attributable to testing. A request to fix a discovered defect produces a separately scoped next step rather than a silent product edit or automatic workflow launch.

### MT-002: Packet And Standalone Entry Contracts

**Behavior.** Establish the explicitly selected skill, entry mode, target/environment, project library identity, requested outcome, expected behavior source, relevant identity/version and execution limits from the invocation and available evidence. Ask through the active host's native question tool only for a material unresolved choice that prevents the next dependent action; missing answers are not consent. Packet and standalone QA follow the entry contracts below; library-based regression follows MT-022 without automatically invoking QA or implementation.

In packet mode, select exactly the requested packet; use its current checklist/handoff as context and retrieve only linked requirement definitions, contracts, dependencies and existing verification evidence needed for that packet. Validate pinned specification and technical-agreement state through existing read-only scenario capabilities. Read workflow manifest/decisions/catalog/experience only through their owning scenario MCP, never direct YAML readers or parsers. Do not start/complete a product task, take implementation ownership, update plan/checklist/handoff, migrate legacy state or choose another packet. Missing/stale authoritative inputs or a missing matching capability prevent a packet-conformance verdict and require an explicit blocker, not a silent switch to standalone mode. Safe independent observations may still be recorded as such without claiming packet conformance.

In standalone mode, use the named URL, endpoint, CLI, repository feature or other concrete target and the user's expected outcome or accessible authoritative documentation. Do not require a specification, plan, Git or workflow MCP solely because packet mode uses them. If the oracle is unknown, distinguish exploratory observations from verified requirement compliance; clarify material ambiguity rather than invent behavior. An unrelated project or the host GUI is not an implicit target.

**Acceptance.** A selected packet uses only its linked scope and reports stale pins without changing workflow state. The same deployed URL can be tested in standalone mode with no planning bundle. Ambiguous competing targets or an unknown expected outcome prompt the missing decision; unavailable MCP never triggers handwritten workflow YAML or an unsupported conformance pass.

### MT-003: Determine Actual Implementation And Target Identity

**Behavior.** Before choosing tests, make a bounded inventory of requested behaviors and actually present surfaces. Reconcile the selected criteria with current source/configuration when available, scoped tracked/staged/untracked changes when Git is available, served routes/operations and actual runtime observations. Git is useful evidence, not a clean-tree or commit prerequisite. Preserve unrelated work.

For each requested behavior distinguish **implemented**, **partial**, **not implemented** or **unknown**, with evidence and uncertainty. A plan, checked box, file name, stub, successful build or previous narrative is not proof of live implementation. Keep implementation presence separate from test success. Verify the actual origin, application and relevant build/version as far as the environment exposes them. A listening port or generic HTTP success does not prove target identity. A mismatched deployment blocks affected conformance checks; do not start a replacement server or pretend the local checkout is what the browser serves. If the exact version is not observable, report that limit rather than inventing it.

**Acceptance.** A packet with an implemented API but a missing UI is classified per surface rather than wholly implemented. A different service on the expected port is not tested as the target. A confirmed missing required feature is reported as a failed criterion; lack of access or inconclusive identity is reported as blocked/uncertain rather than a fabricated defect or success.

### MT-004: Risk-Based Manual Charter And Capability Routing

**Behavior.** Before scenario execution, create an explicit test plan and concrete test cases, using any acceptance criteria actually supplied from the selected planning packet. QA first searches/reuses the project library and maintains definitions under MT-018 through MT-020; regression loads its pinned selection under MT-022 rather than recreating cases. The compact charter covers each applicable requested criterion: stable case identity/revision, behavior/requirement, risk and priority, preconditions/data, observation surface, actions or request, expected result, cleanup and required/optional status. Standalone cases use the available request/oracle without inventing nonexistent packet criteria. Prioritize core user outcomes, changed boundaries and high-impact failures, then material negative, boundary and recovery cases. Include relevant invariants, permissions, state transitions, compatibility and absence guarantees. Do not expand a bounded request to a whole-application crawl, impose a bug quota or drop required criteria for speed. Mark true exclusions with a reason, not as successful checks.

Discover already available permitted capabilities through the host's exposed tool schemas. Use browser tools for real web interaction/visual claims; a direct URL or HTTP client for API behavior; available native commands for CLI/tooling; and a combination only when it proves a meaningful boundary. Use repository-native commands only when they actually exist. Native or other non-web targets require a suitable available interaction capability; do not force them through a browser. If an equivalent authorized tool exists, use it; otherwise block the affected check without installing anything or inventing a callable tool. Source inspection, a screenshot alone or a passing unit-test command cannot substitute for an unavailable interactive check.

**Acceptance.** API-only input selects direct HTTP without launching a browser or loading web-only guidance. A UI criterion selects live browser interaction even when API/unit checks pass. Missing browser capability leaves UI criteria blocked while independent permitted API checks can continue. Every requested criterion remains visible in the charter and final coverage.

### MT-005: User-Visible Web Verification

**Behavior.** For selected web behavior, inspect the live page before acting and use observed accessible names/roles, stable references or verified locators rather than guessed controls. Refresh stale references after navigation or substantial DOM changes. Check the user's meaningful outcome, not only a click's successful execution. Use bounded waits for a specific state, text, URL, element or response; do not use blanket network-idle or arbitrary sleeps as correctness evidence.

Exercise the relevant happy path and risk-justified invalid, empty, loading, error and recovery states. For relevant interactions, inspect keyboard access, focus, labels, error feedback and visible usability. Check responsive layouts and browser/device differences only to the extent required by target support or the request; record the actual browser/viewport used and untested combinations. Console/network observations support diagnosis but do not replace visible behavior or establish that the whole application is error-free. A screenshot supports a visual observation but does not prove behavior or a full accessibility audit.

**Acceptance.** A control that accepts a click but fails to produce the expected visible/persisted result does not pass. A delayed result is observed within the recorded wait bound rather than immediately declared absent or retried indefinitely. A keyboard-only failure has concrete focus/action evidence; testing one viewport is not reported as all-device coverage.

### MT-006: Direct API And Cross-Boundary Verification

**Behavior.** Use the correct verified origin, path, method, query/body, content type and authorized authentication context. Prefer direct HTTP over browser navigation for nontrivial API requests. Validate the promised status, material headers, payload shape/values and relevant resulting state, not merely successful transport, a `2xx` status or parseable JSON. Include material invalid input, boundary, permission and error cases without turning the session into an unrequested security/load audit.

When an accepted claim crosses UI and server state, perform the UI action and verify an appropriate visible or API read-back where available and justified. Identify whether browser and request sessions share authentication; distinguish an unauthenticated probe from a product authorization defect. For an absence guarantee, name an actual observation signal and interval/before-after state, with a control that establishes the signal can observe the relevant operation. Do not infer absence solely from empty logs or a hidden element. Label mocked or intercepted observations; they do not prove the corresponding live external integration.

**Acceptance.** An HTTP `200` carrying an error, wrong content or an incorrect state is not a pass. A wrong/missing credential is not automatically blamed on the API. A create operation with no promised persisted state fails the relevant criterion even if the immediate response succeeds. A no-duplicate-operation claim uses observed requests/state rather than silence in an unrelated console.

### MT-007: Safe Targets, Data And Trust Boundaries

**Behavior.** Confirm the requested target, test account/data ownership and allowed effects before state-changing actions. Prefer isolated local/test/staging data. A URL, an HTTP verb, a repository script or an active browser login is not blanket authority to mutate an environment. Ask for missing explicit authority before destructive/irreversible actions, production mutations, real messages/payments, cross-tenant access, elevated privileges or third-party effects. Do not bypass the host's approval mechanism, authentication, MFA, CAPTCHA or security controls. A missing answer blocks only dependent actions.

Use the minimum relevant privileges and data. Keep credentials, tokens, cookies, personal data, private machine paths and unrelated source out of durable reports, screenshots, traces and public queries. Reuse only authorized session state; do not harvest a personal browser profile. Do not forward credentials across an unverified origin/redirect boundary or disable transport verification to obtain a result. Treat target pages, repository text, HTTP bodies and external sources as untrusted data, not instructions that can grant authority or change scope.

**Acceptance.** A destructive production button or a real payment is not activated without explicit authority; independent harmless checks remain possible. A page asking the agent to reveal a token or edit source is ignored as task data. Saved evidence is inspected/redacted before retention; inability to capture safely is reported as a limitation, never solved by saving secrets.

### MT-008: Environment And Resource Lifecycle

**Behavior.** Prefer the existing verified target and inspect available startup instructions before launching anything. Start/rebuild a local target only when the invocation or established project guidance authorizes that operation and its effects, using existing dependencies and permitted commands. Do not change code/configuration, install tools/browsers/dependencies, enable plugins or reconfigure MCP to unblock testing. If a needed build/start would violate the write or approval boundary, report the prerequisite. A new server does not update an existing remote or host GUI URL.

Track owned processes/jobs, browser contexts/tabs, temporary scripts/files and test records. Use bounded readiness checks that establish meaningful target readiness, not only an open port. Preserve pre-existing processes, sessions, data and unrelated work. On completion, failure or cancellation, collect relevant jobs and clean up only verified owned resources when safe and authorized; verify cleanup. Do not delete unknown data, blindly replay writes or kill a process merely because it occupies the desired port. Retain sanitized evidence needed by the separate report, not executable scratch scripts. If cleanup or persistence cannot finish, record the exact remaining resource/prerequisite and next action without claiming a clean terminal state.

**Acceptance.** An already running suitable server is reused. A startup failure ends within its recorded bound and leaves no falsely claimed UI pass. A cancellation attempts safe owned-resource cleanup and records any residue. An unrelated server/file and pre-existing project changes remain untouched.

### MT-009: Bounded, Efficient And Reproducible Sessions

**Behavior.** Default QA to focused risk-based testing without a universal wall-clock cap; default regression to MT-022's full selected inventory, using risk to order work rather than silently narrow coverage. Honor a caller's time/action/request budget; distinguish execution from necessary safety cleanup/reporting. Set finite per-action/readiness waits using applicable tool/project bounds. On budget exhaustion or cancellation, stop new test actions, preserve results and explicitly mark remaining required cases not run. Never downgrade them to optional or infer success.

Use at most one diagnostic reproduction of a product failure/uncertain observation by default, with controlled preconditions and recorded attempts; allow more only for an explicit request or a documented target-specific reason within budget. This is not a limit on correcting broken execution scripts: MT-016 requires repairing and rerunning those until their correctness is established or a concrete budget/prerequisite prevents it. Do not repeat a state-changing operation without confirming its safety/idempotency. Keep intermittent product failures and their observed frequency; a later success does not erase the first failure. Continue independent safe checks after a case failure; do not cascade through invalid preconditions.

Minimize duplicated discovery, whole-spec reads, context and tool calls: load only mode/surface-relevant references, reuse unchanged exact evidence only at its owning boundary, group independent observations where safe, and collect expensive traces/video only when needed. Plan and generate the necessary temporary code, then delegate routine execution and waiting to native jobs under MT-017, not a model-driven loop of individual actions, sleeps or log polling. Do not run unrelated full repository suites, install tools, research the internet or delegate parallel agent sessions unconditionally; full regression still executes its explicitly selected case inventory. Record elapsed time and available action/request counts with coverage/limitations; do not claim an unmeasured speedup or literally zero tokens for planning, code generation and analysis. Correctness, authorization, privacy and coverage outrank fewer calls.

**Acceptance.** A caller budget ending after the smoke scenario leaves remaining cases visibly not run and the overall result incomplete. A failure followed by one successful diagnostic repeat remains recorded. An API-only short-path run performs no irrelevant browser setup or web-reference loading. Changed source/environment/session state invalidates affected reused evidence instead of preserving a stale pass.

### MT-010: Separate Durable Report And Evidence

**Behavior.** Save one separate human-readable Markdown report per invocation and give a concise chat summary linking to it and the identified workspace run. Also provide the required upstream Allure Report result/view artifacts under MT-032/MT-033; Allure does not silently replace the Markdown summary or canonical run data. Prefer an explicit caller location, then a safe established reporting convention. Otherwise use a new unique run directory: `docs/specs/<slug>/testing/<run-id>/report.md` for a packet and `docs/testing/<run-id>/report.md` for a standalone project. A URL-only target uses the session's authorized writable local output directory. These are run/report outputs, not planning/profile contracts or an independently editable machine schema. Validate destinations/ownership, preserve previous reports and user edits, and avoid unsafe path/symlink traversal. A materially conflicting or unavailable destination requires clarification or an explicit persistence blocker, not overwriting another artifact.

The report records skill/mode and target identity/build uncertainty; project library and case/suite IDs with their tested revisions; packet/requirement or standalone oracle references; actual hosts/environments, browser/viewport/authentication role without secrets; the test plan and cases; per-case actions/input, expected/actual observation, status and evidence; implementation inventory; background job outcomes and script-health/repair results separately from product findings; severity-ranked bugs with preconditions and reproducible steps sufficient for correction; intermittent observations; required coverage gaps and reasons; elapsed time/budget and available operation counts; scheduling/resource decisions and measured versus estimated usage where relevant; library updates/persistence status and automation recommendations; owned-resource cleanup outcome; and concrete next actions/known owners. Distinguish observed facts, inference and unknowns. Keep evidence bounded, relevant, redacted and linked to the corresponding case/finding; preserve it long enough for the saved report to remain usable. Prefer minimal screenshots or response excerpts, with trace/video only when useful.

For a failure, capture enough evidence when discovered that later cleanup or a retry cannot erase it. Do not save raw credentials, unbounded logs, unrelated source or scratch scripts as report evidence. If a report cannot be saved, provide available results in chat, state persistence is incomplete and identify the prerequisite; a chat message is not a saved-report pass. Never update packet/checklist/handoff, product workflow status or specification decisions as a side effect of reporting.

**Acceptance.** Repeated invocations create distinguishable reports without overwriting earlier findings. A reported UI/API defect has expected/actual behavior, a bounded reproduction and usable redacted evidence linked to its case revision. Project/workflow diffs show only authorized library/run-metadata and reporting writes, with no package-status or source/test changes. Read-only output failure preserves observations in chat and leaves report/library persistence explicitly incomplete.

### MT-011: Honest Verdicts And Ownership Separation

**Behavior.** Use case outcomes **PASS**, **FAIL**, **BLOCKED**, **NOT_RUN**, **INCONCLUSIVE** and **NOT_APPLICABLE** with explicit meanings: observed expected behavior; confirmed violated applicable expectation; missing prerequisite/authority/capability; not executed; insufficient/ambiguous evidence; and genuinely outside applicable scope with justification. Never use not-applicable for a missing required implementation or unavailable tool. Root-cause confidence is separate from a confirmed observed violation.

Summarize **FAILED** if any applicable case has a confirmed product violation, including an observed intermittent violation; otherwise **INCOMPLETE** if any required case is blocked, not run or inconclusive, the selected regression inventory is not fully accounted for, required execution scripts have unresolved errors, a relevant job has not been collected in a terminal state, or required report/library persistence or cleanup is incomplete; otherwise **PASSED** for the stated scope only. If there are no applicable executed checks, the result cannot be passed. Preserve script/infrastructure errors and coverage gaps alongside product findings. Optional gaps are limitations, not failures by themselves. An absence of findings is not proof of untested behavior, complete security/accessibility compliance or production readiness.

Report reproduction and next action without fixing product code or claiming another workflow's completion. Suggested regression tests are recommendations for implementation, not tests authored by this skill. When a case has no bug, proceed to the next case within the selected scope. After the entire selected scope, provide the report, explicitly say when no bugs were found, and stop; do not automatically select the next planning packet or development stage. A passing manual report neither closes a packet automatically nor replaces its original required implementation checks.

**Acceptance.** Passing API cases plus blocked required UI cases yield incomplete, not passed. A confirmed defect plus blocked cases yields failed with both the defect and gaps visible. An all-excluded or empty session does not pass. No verdict mutates packet/product state or silently launches a fix.

### MT-012: Repeat, Resume And Interrupted Runs

**Behavior.** A fresh invocation can retest an earlier report's findings, but revalidate target identity, permissions, state and affected criteria before reusing evidence. Preserve earlier reports; distinguish a current reproduced/fixed observation from historical evidence. Do not infer a fix from a changed file or a previous successful attempt. On interruption or a deliberate background-wait checkpoint, save available observations, project/library snapshot identity, selected case revisions, plan/dependency/resource reservations, owned host/stand/job identities, expected outputs and cleanup/persistence state; on resume, reconnect to actual jobs/resources and revalidate current inputs, authority and capacity before continuing. Do not duplicate a still-running job, blindly repeat non-idempotent actions or treat an incomplete report as a completed run. A background wait is not cancellation: do not kill a healthy owned test batch merely to end a chat turn.

**Acceptance.** After a deployment or authentication change, affected checks are freshly observed. Resuming after a possibly successful POST uses safe read-back before any replay. The old failure remains discoverable, the new report links its fresh result, and uncollected resources are not falsely claimed removed.

### MT-013: Portable Packaging And Shared Discipline

**Behavior.** Preserve one authoritative template source per skill and generate isolated Codex, Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness artifacts under the collection's existing conventions. Both skills remain explicit-only in each host's supported metadata, use the active host's actual callable question/tool schemas and only declared host substitutions, and do not hard-code generated MCP namespaces. The separate testing workspace runtime and both skills share one authoritative library/protocol semantics source, packaged or referenced consistently through compatible declared contracts rather than independently maintained host versions or direct storage bypasses. Diagnose missing/incompatible testing-runtime capabilities without automatic installation or registration. Standalone use must not acquire a dependency on an installed planning workflow; the separate testing-runtime prerequisite does not make engineering-workflow MCP mandatory outside packet conformance under MT-002. Matching shared guidance must be self-contained in the installed artifact and verified through the existing engineering-manual contract; do not fetch, approximate or maintain a competing copy when it is missing/incompatible.

Keep discovery text within 240 Unicode code points and the complete main skill document within 4,096 UTF-8 bytes. Keep unconditional authority/routing/reporting rules in the main instructions and conditionally load detailed packet/browser/API/other-surface guidance only when relevant. Preserve root shared ownership of engineering/test discipline. Apply its behavior-focused observations, failure honesty and discrimination contextually; manual testing must not fabricate RED/GREEN/PROVE history or mutate project code to demonstrate an assertion. Repository-defined source changes, persistent regression tests and any required implementation mutation checks remain implementation responsibilities.

Do not add a project-specific lifecycle CLI, automatic installation, global configuration changes, publication or project-scoped skill installation/lifecycle mutations inside consuming projects. This does not prohibit explicitly authorized test-library/report metadata writes in the tested project. Preserve the existing pinned global lifecycle and separate-host isolation policies; no actual installation is authorized by this specification.

**Acceptance.** Generated artifacts for all three hosts validate explicit-only invocation, size bounds and absence of foreign-host metadata. A standalone session with complete installed skill resources and available compatible testing capabilities works without planning artifacts or engineering-workflow MCP; missing testing-runtime capability is disclosed rather than automatically installed. A packet session reports a missing conditional prerequisite honestly. A missing/incompatible shared bundle stops dependent work rather than downloading or reconstructing guidance. Validation of the skill does not edit real global user/client state.

### MT-014: Evidence-Based Delivery And Quality Evaluation

**Behavior.** Use the scoped primary-source research recorded in [research.md](docs/specs/testing-and-verification/research.md) and [regression-research.md](docs/specs/testing-and-verification/regression-research.md) to inform both skills: reconnaissance before action, meaningful observation surfaces, isolated authorized state, bounded condition waits, economical evidence, owned lifecycle, stable reusable cases separate from run outcomes, complete inventory enumeration, dependency/isolation-aware scheduling and progressive disclosure. Do not copy unsafe upstream defaults or claim measured superiority from published examples alone.

Before delivery, evaluate the future skill against discriminating scenarios covering both entry paths, actual versus merely planned implementation, browser/API/mixed routing, incorrect payload despite HTTP success, missing tools and stale packet inputs, permission gates, secret redaction, intermittent failure, budget/cancellation, cleanup/report failure, repeat/resume and no unauthorized writes/status changes. Also cover plan-before-script-before-run ordering, broken script repair/rerun, successful exit with missing case output, distinction between script errors and product bugs, multiple background jobs finishing out of order, long-wait checkpoint/resumption without polling or duplicate execution, and the no-bugs scoped continuation rule.

Include an API-only short path that rejects unnecessary browser/setup/context work and a mixed-surface case that rejects false success when one required check is blocked. Also evaluate durable case reuse without duplicates, complete suite expansion and paginated inventory, optimistic conflicts/interrupted writes, schema mismatch, stale expectations, active versus retired cases, recommendation versus confirmed automation, dependency cycles/exclusive data, one versus multiple stands, shared local/remote physical hosts, low/stale/unknown RAM metrics, changing pressure, admission without oversubscription, infrastructure OOM/cancellation, lost remote ownership and recovery without duplicate execution. A synthetic library with at least 1,000 cases and 100 suites is a validation fixture, not a claim about customer scale: a targeted query/lookup must return bounded metadata and selected case bodies without importing all unrelated case content into model context.

Verify mandatory native workflow orchestration in Harness and an established equivalent in Codex/Claude Code, with background execution remaining the scenario execution layer. A missing required workflow capability must block affected execution, not silently fall back to background-only scripts or claim success. Detailed workflow design stays in planning; neither mandatory orchestration nor this verification permits a new model agent for every routine case.

Validate templates and all three generated host distributions with existing repository checks, using isolated fixtures rather than real global configurations. Add discriminating workspace/API/UI/report scenarios for MT-027 through MT-037 while observing MT-028: development execution is Linux/Google Chrome only, with other required platforms explicitly unverified rather than mandatory extra native gates. This platform limit does not remove the three host contracts or authorize a fake native-workflow trace. Record actual checks/results, exact runtime/browser versions, scenario coverage, time and available operation counts; simulated fixture answers are not user consent or live-product evidence. No percentage speedup or exhaustive coverage claim is required or allowed without measurement.

This specification is the behavioral handoff, not an implementation packet or authorization to create the skill now. Planning requires its own explicit invocation after specification readiness; implementation follows separately authorized packets. No commit, installation, publication or real-target testing is implied by this specification run.

**Acceptance.** A delivery report identifies which structural and behavioral scenarios actually ran and which were unavailable, without calling missing evidence a pass. Short-path efficiency is demonstrated by its operation/reference trace while all required observations remain represented. The current invocation ends with specification/research/review evidence only and a clear separate planning next step, with no skill implementation or global mutation.

### MT-015: Plan, Cases, Temporary Code, Execution, Report

**Behavior.** Enforce this observable sequence: (1) establish the target and prepare the test plan and test cases; (2) develop the necessary temporary scripts/code, launch them through MT-017, collect and verify their results, and repair execution-script errors under MT-016; (3) provide the testing report so product bugs can be corrected. Bounded discovery/readiness inspection may inform the plan, but must not become unplanned scenario execution or a model-driven walkthrough of the whole target.

When acceptance criteria are present in a supplied planning packet, QA derives cases from those exact criteria and retains traceability. Do not assume criteria that were not supplied or accessible; use the standalone/request oracle or explicitly mark the missing packet evidence under MT-002. Search/reuse or create and validate the durable case/suite definitions under MT-018 through MT-020 before execution; record subsequent results separately. Regression reuses its existing pinned case definitions rather than authoring a replacement library. Each case has preconditions, actions/input, expected observation, execution method and relevant cleanup. The plan identifies dependencies, independent batches, required coverage and stop conditions before execution. No separate customer approval of each routine plan/script is required when authority and expected behavior are already established. If required library persistence fails, report the blocker and never claim a fully completed run or saved reusable cases; safe independent observations may still be preserved.

Develop enough temporary code to execute and observe the selected scenarios without the model manually issuing each routine action. Use already available permitted browser/HTTP/runtime capabilities; temporary code may orchestrate live browser actions and HTTP calls, collect observations and produce bounded case results. It does not authorize project-code edits, a permanent test suite, invented callable APIs, new dependencies or bypassed interaction/approval gates. Where a required capability cannot be driven through a permitted native scripted/batch mechanism, report that execution prerequisite instead of silently replacing the method with a token-heavy manual loop or faking execution.

**Acceptance.** An execution trace shows a completed plan/case set before scenario code and a prepared script before its test job starts. Supplied packet acceptance criteria map to actual cases and results; absent criteria are not fabricated. A ready temporary scenario runs without a separate model turn for every browser click/HTTP request. The final report includes both reproducible product bugs and explicit clean/incomplete outcomes as applicable.

### MT-016: Correct Execution Scripts Without Hiding Product Bugs

**Behavior.** Check that every necessary script actually launched and reached the intended observations, with its terminal status and expected case outputs accounted for. Distinguish script/infrastructure failures (such as syntax/runtime errors, broken locators, an invalid driver or missing output) from an executed assertion exposing incorrect product behavior. Exit success alone does not prove that cases ran; nonzero exit alone does not identify the product as defective. Expected product failures may be represented by a nonzero status, but the report must still establish the driver's valid execution and captured observations.

For a script error, inspect bounded diagnostics, correct the temporary script, rerun it through the background/equivalent mechanism, and verify the new results. Continue the correction cycle while a correctable execution error remains, within the caller's budget and actual capabilities; do not stop merely because the ordinary product-reproduction allowance was used. Do not blindly rerun unchanged code against a known missing prerequisite. If correction is blocked, cancelled or out of budget, preserve the failed attempts and mark affected verification incomplete with the exact next action. Reconcile possible side effects before any rerun and do not duplicate already completed non-idempotent work.

Never weaken a correct expected result, swallow an exception, omit a failed case or alter product code to obtain a green script. A script/assertion may change only when source requirements or concrete evidence establish that the check itself was wrong; record the reason and preserve earlier evidence. A genuine product bug is reported for correction through the implementation workflow, not repaired by changing its test driver to accept the bug.

**Acceptance.** A syntax-broken temporary script is corrected, rerun and its intended case outputs verified. A runner that exits zero but emits no expected case results leaves verification incomplete. A correctly executed HTTP check observing a wrong payload remains a product failure rather than prompting a weakened assertion. An unavailable runtime is reported as a prerequisite without repeated identical launches or an automatic install.

### MT-017: Native Background Execution And Event-Driven Waiting

**Behavior.** Regression execution must remain under the workflow orchestration required by MT-022; background scripts/jobs are its execution layer, not a replacement for that orchestration. Launch prepared scenario scripts through the active host's actual background-job capability (for example, the capability referred to by the user as `background.job`) or an equivalent native scripted/batch executor. Discover the exposed names/schemas; that example is not a hard-coded callable. The mechanism must execute routine scenario steps and waits without model inference for each operation. Track every owned job with its target, case batch, temporary inputs, expected outputs and cleanup ownership. Keep shared-state-dependent cases ordered; parallel execution is allowed only for independent authorized batches.

For a long-running batch, save a resumable checkpoint, provide a concise running/waiting status and yield/end the current chat turn through the host's supported pending/background lifecycle. Do not represent this as completed testing. Leave healthy test jobs running, do not spend model turns on sleeps, rapid polling, repeated logs or progress-only reasoning, and continue test analysis only after all jobs in the current batch are terminal. Prefer native completion notifications or a native blocking wait that consumes no model turns while pending. Respect any host requirement to collect results before ending a response: use its supported wait/suspension mechanism rather than violating that rule. If detached wake-up/yield is unavailable, state that limit and use an available native blocking wait; if neither mechanism exists, leave execution blocked rather than promise an automatic continuation the host cannot provide.

After completion notification/resumption, collect terminal status and bounded results for every relevant job, including jobs that failed, were cancelled or finished out of order. Do not duplicate running jobs or continue from the first successful job while another required job is pending. Only then diagnose script failures, launch necessary corrected jobs, or finalize the testing report. A correction batch repeats the same wait/collect boundary. Before a completed-testing answer, no relevant job may remain unaccounted for; cancellation and resource cleanup follow MT-008 and MT-012. Tokens are necessarily used for planning, code generation, repair and analysis, but not for simulating script execution or active waiting; do not claim a measured cost saving without evidence.

**Acceptance.** Two test jobs finishing out of order produce no completed-testing report until both terminal results are collected. A long job causes one pending checkpoint and native waiting/notification, not repeated model polling turns; resume reconnects to the original job rather than relaunching it. A failed script leads to a corrected background run and a new collection boundary. An unavailable notification/yield facility is reported honestly, with native blocking wait used if available; unavailable execution/wait capability is not presented as a successful run.

### MT-018: Per-Project Durable Library And QA Maintenance

**Behavior.** Each tested project owns a separate canonical durable library of reusable test cases and suites shared by its QA/regression workflows and the workspace UI/MCP. Establish project identity and authorized location explicitly or from verified project conventions; do not infer that the collection repository or current directory owns an unrelated URL-only target. The local workspace runtime may expose explicitly opened project libraries without mixing their identities, permissions, definitions or runs; it must not silently create a shared cross-project/team service. The separate workspace package is required under MT-027, while physical files/database/layout remain planning decisions. Its declared operations mediate canonical state; clients must not maintain editable shadow libraries or bypass revision/authority checks with raw storage writes.

QA searches existing definitions before creating cases, reuses matching IDs, and maintains the cases/suites it plans and checks. Save validated definitions, including failed or blocked scenarios rather than only successful ones; preserve which cases were actually executed. Missing or ambiguous oracles can remain clearly non-ready drafts, not invented active acceptance criteria. Product behavior is not the authority for silently changing expected results: trace updates to requirements/user instructions and mark stale definitions when that authority cannot be established. Case maintenance and run-result persistence are separate operations; failure of either required operation remains explicit.

**Acceptance.** A fresh session can locate and rerun a previously checked case without conversation history or the old temporary script. A second QA pass reuses the case instead of creating a title-based duplicate. A failed product scenario remains in the library with its intended expectation and a separate failed run result. Two projects never receive each other's cases through an inferred default location.

### MT-019: Stable Cases, Suites And Revision-Linked Results

**Behavior.** Case definitions have stable project-scoped identity and revision, title/purpose, lifecycle/readiness, requirement or standalone oracle references, searchable feature/surface/tags/priority, preconditions and authorized data/account references, concrete actions/inputs and expected observations, environment applicability, cleanup, dependencies/exclusive resources, execution/automation references and relevant duration/resource estimates with provenance or an explicit unknown value. Keep secrets and raw personal data out of definitions. Human-readable names are not identity; renames preserve references/history. Estimate, observed measurement and assumption must remain distinguishable.

Suites have stable identity/revision, purpose/selection metadata and unambiguous case membership/order constraints. Reference canonical cases rather than duplicating their bodies. Expansion is finite and validates references; the same case selected through multiple suites executes once per intended parameter/environment variant unless repetition is explicit. Reject duplicate IDs, dangling references, contradictory ordering and invalid case content instead of silently repairing expectations.

Run results are separate from definitions and identify run, project/library snapshot, case/suite revision, target build/environment, execution method, observation/verdict, evidence and relevant resource/runtime facts. A latest-result view is derived from identified runs, not an editable replacement of history. Changing a case never retroactively changes what an earlier run checked. Lifecycle (active or retired) is distinct from readiness (ready, draft/non-ready or stale): an active but non-ready case remains visible to full regression as a blocked prerequisite, not an invisible exclusion. A failing run alone never retires a case.

**Acceptance.** Renaming a case preserves suite membership and historical results. Editing its expected outcome creates a new identifiable revision without rewriting old evidence. Selecting overlapping suites does not duplicate an unintended destructive action. A missing case reference or duplicate identity produces a visible validation issue rather than a silently incomplete suite.

### MT-020: Search, Navigation And Complete Enumeration

**Behavior.** Provide agent-friendly discovery by exact case/suite ID and bounded metadata search/filtering by relevant title/text, feature/surface/tags, requirement, suite membership, lifecycle, automation state and available recent-result references. Show enough summary to choose the right definitions, then retrieve their exact full content on demand. Do not load every case body, unrelated product specification or execution log to answer a targeted lookup. Physical indexing/query implementation is not prescribed.

Library metadata and any derived index must identify the source revision, detect stale/missing/corrupt references, and never become a competing editable source of case truth. A permitted repair can rebuild derived navigation from canonical validated definitions; it cannot invent missing cases or discard edits. Full enumeration must expose and follow every bounded continuation and establish an internally consistent inventory, not just trust the first search page or a count. Pin each enumeration/exact-body continuation to one retained immutable source/query/revision. Unrelated result appends must not invalidate that available read or mix newer pages into it; disclose current-source drift separately. Missing, incompatible or corrupt pinned data blocks the affected claim, never silently restarts on the current source. Reconcile changed state before claiming current coverage or applying stale writes; a readable historical snapshot does not authorize a stale mutation.

**Acceptance.** In the MT-014 fixture, an exact lookup or filtered query returns bounded summaries and selected bodies without reading all unrelated bodies into model context. Full regression includes cases beyond the first page. A stale index cannot hide an active case or produce an unqualified full-coverage pass. Rebuilding navigation preserves case IDs, revisions, content and run history.

### MT-021: Automation Recommendations, Not QA Autotest Authoring

**Behavior.** QA proposes useful cases/suites for permanent automation using recurrence, regression risk, determinism, execution cost, maintenance burden and already available project coverage. Link each proposal to case/suite IDs and revisions, the behavior to preserve, suggested owning test layer/observation and expected benefit/limits. A proposal is not an approval, implementation task, new test file or confirmed coverage.

The implementation executor, acting under the appropriate implementation authority, decides whether/how to automate and may add permanent autotests to the tested project. QA does not make that decision on the executor's behalf, invoke implementation automatically or add persistent tests itself. Distinguish proposed, explicitly decided and actually implemented automation using available decision/reference evidence; do not infer a decision from silence or a temporary script's success. Link existing implemented automation only after verifying its location/entrypoint and case mapping. Regression can execute that authorized automation and temporary drivers for the remaining cases without changing the application or permanent tests.

**Acceptance.** A repeatedly checked suite yields a concrete case-linked recommendation but no test/source edit or fabricated accepted status. A subsequently implemented autotest can be linked to its actual covered case revisions. Running one green suite does not mark unmapped/manual cases automated or tested. The implementation executor retains the automation decision.

### MT-022: Separate Regression Invocation And Full-Scope Semantics

**Behavior.** `regression-testing` is a separate explicit invocation. It requires the selected project's compatible library and authorized targets, not a fresh planning packet or prior QA conversation.

Workflow orchestration is an explicit requirement, not an optional implementation choice. In DeepSeek Harness, use the actual native workflow capability exposed by the host (normally the `workflow` tool); in Codex and Claude Code, use an equivalent workflow-orchestration mechanism whose real capabilities and integration planning establishes. Preserve the same scope, lifecycle, result-collection and safety contracts across hosts; do not invent an unavailable tool or silently substitute a background-only script, an ad hoc agent loop or a plain test command for the required orchestration. An unavailable required workflow mechanism blocks the affected regression execution; it never produces a pass. Planning owns phase structure, parameters, host-specific mechanisms and the interaction between workflow, agents and background jobs. This requirement does not authorize Harness/plugin/MCP changes, automatic installation, named-command registration or an unconditional model-agent invocation for every case.

A missing library prompts its location/population prerequisite rather than automatically launching QA or claiming an empty pass. Default full regression inventories all active (non-retired) cases at a recorded coherent snapshot, including cases without permanent automation and active draft/stale cases; an explicitly requested subset is labeled as such. Non-ready selected cases are blocked, not silently excluded or executed against invented expectations. Show retired/inapplicable records and reasons separately rather than hiding their existence or silently executing obsolete expectations.

Freeze the selected IDs/revisions, suite expansion, applicable environment variants and known exclusions before execution. Validate expected behavior against available source freshness and target identity. Every selected applicable case receives a terminal observation or explicit blocked/not-run/inconclusive reason, even if its script, tool, authorization, environment or dependency is unavailable. Do not equate all discovered autotest files, a passing command or one page of metadata with all cases. Preserve the denominator and gaps after budget exhaustion or failures. A changed library mid-run does not silently extend or rewrite the frozen run; report drift and require appropriate fresh checks before claiming coverage of the newer inventory.

**Acceptance.** Full regression includes manual/scripted and permanent-automation cases beyond the first metadata page. An unavailable required browser case leaves the regression incomplete while independent API cases can run. A filtered smoke request is never reported as full regression. A library change is traceable to the frozen versus current inventory instead of corrupting the coverage claim.

The execution trace establishes a real native workflow run in DeepSeek Harness or the verified equivalent orchestration on Codex/Claude Code. A direct background-script/test-command run alone does not satisfy this requirement. Missing required workflow capability produces an explicit execution blocker, not a silent fallback or success. Planning describes the concrete stages/parameters/job integration while retaining mandatory workflow use.

### MT-023: Dependency, Isolation And Stand-Aware Scheduling

**Behavior.** Build an execution plan over selected cases/variants, dependencies, data/reset needs, exclusive accounts/resources, available tools, expected cost and authorized stand inventory. Decide which work is sequential or parallel and which cases share one stand or require separate compatible stands. Parallelize only proven independent work within MT-024 capacity; unknown isolation defaults to serialization or a prerequisite blocker, not optimistic concurrency. Cases with unmet/failed prerequisites are blocked rather than executed on invalid state. Cycles or missing dependencies produce concrete affected-case issues; independent safe work may continue.

Stand placement is task-dependent: local, remote or a combination. Stand identity includes actual product/build, configuration, OS/runtime and required tool capabilities, location/physical host, data/account isolation, authority, readiness/reset needs, capacity and ownership. Do not impose a local-only/one-OS assumption on tested stands or claim that an unobserved environment was verified; missing access, identity or required capability blocks affected execution. The workspace tool's implemented-but-unverified support matrix is separately defined by MT-028 and does not establish observations about any stand. Multiple URLs/containers on one host are not independent resource budgets. Separate hosts do not make shared accounts/data independent. Grouping cases onto one worker is not a cross-job/run resource lock: establish exclusive ownership for a required shared resource across cooperating runs, or block conflicting execution. A subset request does not authorize adding outside-scope prerequisites silently.

Reuse appropriate existing stands. Start/reset/stop additional stands only through already available declared operations with established per-run authority, capacity and safe cleanup; do not provision infrastructure or install dependencies merely to improve speed. Explain stand count, case assignment and serialization/parallelism decisions. Minimize unnecessary setup/restarts while preserving case correctness and isolation. Regression orchestration uses the required workflow mechanism under MT-022; its scheduling/execution work runs in temporary/native execution mechanisms, not one new model agent per case.

**Acceptance.** Two state-mutating cases sharing an account are serialized or isolated, while independent read-only cases may run together if capacity permits. A setup failure blocks dependent cases but not an independent safe group. A dependency cycle, unavailable stand or competing owner is explicit. Two stand aliases for one host cannot be used to double the memory allowance.

### MT-024: Resource Admission, RAM Pressure And Runtime Safeguards

**Behavior.** Before admitting work, identify every relevant driver/execution host and managed stand host, including a local browser controlling a remote product. Use fresh available-memory observations and effective host/container/process limits, current usage/reservations, declared headroom for the OS/unrelated workloads, and conservative peak demand for stand, worker, browser and child processes. Keep accounting consistent: neither ignore shared-host allocations nor double-count usage already included in available memory. CPU count, swap space, a soft reservation or worker count alone is not a RAM-safety budget. Other material CPU/process/disk constraints also bound admission where they affect the task.

The plan records measurement sources/freshness, measured versus estimated costs, reserve policy, concurrency/stand limits and finite action/job deadlines. Choose values from caller/project limits, observed workload or bounded safe calibration; do not invent measured peaks. Unknown/stale required capacity or unbounded demand blocks additional managed allocation; concurrency one is not automatically safe. A calibration run is allowed only when its own bounded resource envelope and authority are established. For an existing external target outside the agent's management/telemetry authority, respect the approved request/load budget, account for the agent's own execution hosts and report unavailable remote guarantees; do not pretend to observe/control that server's RAM or provision extra remote stands blindly.

Monitor resource pressure during execution through the native runner/temporary scheduler without model polling. Recheck before new admissions. On low headroom, stale telemetry, exceeded limits or stand loss, stop new admissions and reduce owned concurrency/release idle owned stands when safe. If a running workload threatens its declared envelope, perform bounded graceful cancellation/termination of owned work with checkpointed results; never kill unrelated processes or disable OOM/security protections. Collect every affected job, distinguish infrastructure OOM/cancellation from product failure, preserve incomplete case outcomes and require fresh readiness/capacity before retry. Store observed usage as identified run evidence for future estimates, not invented case truth.

The guarantee is that the workflow does not knowingly over-admit its own bounded workload and reacts to observed pressure. No finite observation can guarantee that arbitrary unrelated host activity will never exhaust memory; disclose that limit rather than claim universal OOM prevention. Use enforceable native limits where available and authorized; missing enforcement/measurement is a recorded prerequisite or limitation, not assumed protection.

**Acceptance.** With 3 GiB currently available, 1 GiB reserved headroom and a proposed 2.5 GiB additional peak, the scheduler does not launch that allocation. Local browser demand counts even when the product is remote. A pressure increase stops pending admissions; affected owned work is safely collected/cancelled without touching unrelated processes. Stale/unknown metrics do not justify an automatic extra stand, and an infrastructure OOM never becomes a product pass. These are deterministic quality scenarios, not claims of measured customer capacity.

### MT-025: Library Integrity, Compatibility, Retention And Recovery

**Behavior.** Validate logical schema/version, identities, references and content before consuming or updating a library. Unsupported/newer or partially migrated formats cannot be silently rewritten, field-dropped or treated as fully tested. Keep common semantics compatible across the two skills and hosts. A migration/rollback that changes authoritative stored data requires separately agreed scope and must preserve identities, valid case history and run references; do not install a storage service or auto-migrate just to start a run.

Updates detect the expected revision of touched definitions and affected relationships. Concurrent edits must not silently overwrite each other; identical repeats are idempotent where applicable, and possible duplicates are reconciled by source/behavior identity, not title alone. A logical update must preserve a valid old or new state or explicitly expose a recoverable interrupted operation, never present mixed/dangling state as success. On a conflict or uncertain write outcome, inspect current exact state before any retry. Planning must explain how the chosen representation and existing project recovery/history mechanisms preserve a recoverable previous valid library; Git is not a runtime prerequisite.

Default to non-destructive lifecycle changes: retire obsolete definitions with provenance rather than deleting cases/history merely because requirements changed or a test failed. Do not automatically purge definitions, decisions or run summaries. Any permanent deletion, migration, evidence-pruning or retention change requires explicit policy/authority; missing old evidence is marked unavailable rather than re-created as a pass. Minimize retained sensitive data under MT-007. Regression appends identified run observations and may flag stale definitions for QA; it does not silently change canonical expectations/lifecycle to obtain green.

**Acceptance.** Concurrent updates from the same old revision yield an explicit conflict, not a lost edit. A failed/interrupted write leaves recoverable validated data and no false saved-library claim. An incompatible schema blocks dependent writes/full-coverage claims. Restoring a prior valid library preserves stable IDs and meaningful run references. A product failure or renamed feature never automatically deletes its case or old evidence.

### MT-026: Planning-Owned Technical Choices And Declared Contracts

**Behavior.** The separate workspace tool and upstream Allure Report reuse are selected outcomes, not options to remove during planning. Planning still details and technically agrees storage/search, public contract realization, compatible upstream versions, concrete limits/timeouts, metric and lifecycle mechanisms and MT-022's mandatory workflow integration on each host. Compare the highest sufficient representation with alternatives only where actual requirements justify them; SQLite, a particular UI framework, internal layout and a separate database service are not selected. Do not pre-create implementation helpers or execute old unaccepted packets from this specification run.

Planning creates exactly the confirmed specification-local contract outputs: `contracts/openapi.yaml` for the local HTTP/UI boundary; `contracts/mcp.md` for testing-runtime capabilities and invocation/error semantics; `contracts/schemas/data.schema.json` for one authoritative validated project/case/suite/revision/run/report model; and `quality/scenarios.yaml` for measurable failure, recovery, concurrency, privacy and resource scenarios. HTTP/MCP projections reference the common semantics rather than create independently editable truths. Reconcile the existing draft schema instead of treating it as approved or adding a competing source. These contracts realize MT-018 through MT-025 and MT-027 through MT-037, including complete inventory, cross-surface conflicts, local access, reporting failures, native host workflow use and MT-028's explicit evidence boundary.

The confirmed project design outputs are `design/system/catalog.yaml`, `design/system/library.penpot`, `design/specs/testing-and-verification/experience.yaml` and `design/specs/testing-and-verification/screens.penpot`. Main planning records their dependencies; separately invoked design planning owns their creation and verified shared-component/screen evidence. No token export or separate architecture DSL is declared. Specification creates none of these contract/design artifacts and does not edit Penpot.

**Acceptance.** The next plan preserves the selected workspace outcome and ready-made Allure viewer, explains storage/reuse tradeoffs and host workflow/job integration, and binds all consumers to compatible public/data contracts. Each declared output maps to observable requirements; quality scenarios distinguish implemented support from the limited native verification scope. Design-dependent packets are not silently executed without required design evidence. Old draft files alone are neither approval nor technical agreement.

### MT-027: Separate Workspace Delivery And Reuse Boundary

**Behavior.** Deliver the testing tool as a separate workspace package in this repository, usable as a local case/run application and through its declared MCP capabilities. Do not move to a separate Git repository or silently fold its business state into the engineering-workflow MCP. Preserve the two skills as clients of compatible declared testing capabilities rather than direct storage writers or independently maintained libraries. The runtime's supported version/capabilities, readiness and missing prerequisites must be discoverable without running tests or changing global configuration.

The first version covers case/suite management and revisions, frozen run scope, results/attachments, a simple UI and basic settings. Separate Shared steps, Defects, TestOps-style CI Jobs and custom Dashboards are deferred from this delivery, not implicitly required or cancelled forever. Native background execution is not the deferred CI Jobs feature. Evaluate suitable open-source components and their licensing/contract fit before implementing uncovered needs; do not assume no open-source case manager exists, require a commercial TestOps subscription or copy proprietary TestOps code/assets. Reuse upstream Allure Report for report rendering. This is not permission to replace its viewer with a new imitation or require an unrelated full TMS stack. Exact dependencies and implementation units remain planning decisions.

An explicit normal application startup entrypoint is allowed; it is not a project-specific installer or replacement for the collection's pinned global skill lifecycle. No automatic package/browsers/renderer download, plugin enablement, MCP registration, migration or publication occurs as a side effect of testing or opening a view. Missing/incompatible capabilities produce a bounded prerequisite report; they do not cause raw-storage bypass, an editable shadow store or a claimed saved run.

**Acceptance.** A user can identify and explicitly start the tool independently of the skill collection's authoring workflows. Compatible skill clients and the UI resolve the same case revision through declared operations. An absent runtime or renderer yields an actionable missing-capability state without an installation or fake success. Dependency/reuse evidence distinguishes upstream code from the integration supplied here.

### MT-028: Implemented Support Versus Development Evidence

**Behavior.** Implement the tool for Linux, Windows and macOS and its UI for stable desktop Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox and Safari. Preserve the three skill hosts under MT-013/MT-022. Handle material paths, permissions, process lifecycle, encodings, browser capabilities and accessible interaction differences through compatible behavior, not a Linux/Chrome-only implementation advertised as portable.

The agreed development execution matrix is Linux and real Google Chrome only. Planning/implementation record exact tested versions, actual checks and unavailable evidence. Chromium alone, simulated OS fixtures, source inspection or a successful build must not be labeled a native Google Chrome/Windows/macOS/other-browser pass. Other required platforms remain supported but explicitly unverified in this cycle; an incompatibility later found there is a defect, not grounds to relabel them unsupported. Do not impose additional native all-platform qualification as a gate to completing this agreed development cycle. Unrun environments outside that matrix are compatibility-evidence limitations, not invented successful cases or extra required executions that automatically invalidate an otherwise complete Linux/Chrome evaluation.

This distinction does not waive missing required Linux/Chrome checks, actual host-orchestration evidence or safety. It does not restrict the task-dependent platforms of applications being tested by the delivered skills. A selected SUT check still needs its actual capability/identity or receives an explicit blocker. Pin chosen dependency/client versions during planning and distinguish tool build/runtime, browser client and tested-target environments; do not infer a universal version/runtime from the developer's machine.

**Acceptance.** A delivery report lists all required support environments, identifies Linux/Google Chrome as the observed matrix and marks the rest unverified. It contains neither fabricated native results nor an extra all-platform test gate. A Chrome-only API without a compatible supported-browser path violates the implementation contract even if the Linux/Chrome check passed.

### MT-029: Explicit Project Access And One Canonical Library

**Behavior.** Opening a project identifies its stable library and authorized data/report location. A repository path or URL can inform discovery but is not by itself identity or write authority. A URL-only project uses an explicitly owned local location; no default assigns it to the collection or whichever directory is current. Show the selected project/library in UI and MCP responses where confusion could change an action. One local tool may open several separate project libraries, but switching does not merge data, reuse another project's authority or silently retarget an in-flight mutation/run.

Definitions and runs have the shared identity/revision semantics of MT-018 through MT-020. UI caches, search indexes, exports and Allure artifacts are derived views, not new editable authorities. A project/library mismatch, missing ownership, unsafe path, invalid schema or unavailable library fails before a dependent write. Do not offer a general filesystem browser/read endpoint, arbitrary command execution or unscoped cross-project search merely because the process has OS permissions. Existing engineering-workflow MCP process permissions are not a new authorization sandbox or proof that this runtime's browser request is allowed.

**Acceptance.** With two opened libraries, a case selected in one cannot be saved into the other through a stale tab, copied identifier or implicit current-project default. A standalone URL retains its explicit library identity across sessions. Missing context shows a prerequisite/selection state, not another project's cases or an automatically initialized unrelated library.

### MT-030: Human And Agent Definition Authoring

**Behavior.** Humans can create, inspect, edit, rename and retire cases/suites in the UI; authorized MCP clients expose the same capabilities. Both apply the same content, oracle, relationship, identity and revision validation. Include MT-019's meaningful fields and MT-020's search/selection semantics without duplicating bodies for suite membership. Keep active/retired lifecycle separate from ready/draft/stale readiness. A human edit creates a new revision with provenance; it does not rewrite old run evidence, silently confirm an unknown oracle or create a permanent SUT autotest.

Mutations carry an expected source/touched revision and an identified retry intent. A stale UI form or MCP write receives a visible conflict rather than overwriting a newer edit. Preserve unsaved input where possible and offer inspection/reload/reconciliation; do not silently merge changed expectations. Double submission or an identical retry must not create duplicate cases or revisions. If the reply is lost, expose operation/effect inspection before a new attempt; uncertainty is not a saved acknowledgment. Invalid input identifies bounded field/relationship issues without coercing away unknown fields or exposing sensitive values. Retirement follows MT-025; no automatic hard deletion or history purge is added.

**Acceptance.** Editing a case in UI and reading it through MCP returns the same new revision. Two writers starting from the same revision do not lose an edit; the loser sees a conflict and retains its proposed content. A repeated create intent creates one case. A failed save remains visibly unsaved, and historical run expectations still show their tested revision.

### MT-031: Frozen Runs, Append-Only Observations And UI State

**Behavior.** The tool records an identified run with the exact project/library snapshot, selected case/suite revisions, variants, targets, prerequisites and exclusions before scenario execution. Full/subset and deduplication rules remain MT-022's; draft/stale active cases retain their blocked place in the denominator. The runtime validates run/observation identity and references, not independent truth of an agent's claimed live observation. Callers remain responsible for valid driver execution, actual evidence and safe effects.

Results/checkpoints retain identified attempts and caller-observed job/resource facts separately from definitions. A stored handle or reservation is not proof of current ownership or permission. Expose whether execution is pending/running/waiting/interrupted/terminal and separately MT-011's authoritative verdict and persistence/cleanup gaps; a cached UI state or successful API response cannot turn unknown live jobs into terminal passes. Finalization accounts for every selected execution and relevant job, failed/cancelled attempts and required outputs. Correctable driver errors follow MT-016, not automatic product blame. Historical observations are not edited into success after a case change or later repeat.

The UI provides run listing/detail, case/attempt outcomes, evidence and frozen-versus-current revision information. It does not launch SUT actions, become a CI scheduler, automatically resume jobs or claim packet completion. Explicit skill/native workflow execution remains the execution owner. Reopening a run revalidates actual jobs/authority/capacity before continuation; it does not blindly replay non-idempotent work.

**Acceptance.** A mid-run case edit leaves the old run on its frozen revision with visible drift. Missing output after exit zero and an uncollected job prevent a completed pass. An active non-ready case stays visible as blocked. Opening a historical run without an agent shows saved observations and uncertainty, not an invented fresh execution.

### MT-032: Upstream Allure View And Semantic Fidelity

**Behavior.** Produce compatible Allure input/results and use the actual ready-made upstream Allure Report viewer for the selected supported version. Do not substitute a home-grown report that merely resembles it. Link exports to the canonical project/run snapshot, exact tested case revision, variant and attempt/evidence identity. Stable case/history identity must not depend on a temporary script path, random run-local name or secrets; distinguish genuinely different variants and runs without conflating retries with new coverage. Preserve upstream licensing/required notices when packaging reused code.

The canonical six case outcomes and three overall verdicts remain authoritative. Preserve the original status, reason, attempts, script-health classification, required gaps, missing outputs, persistence and cleanup facts even when an upstream format has fewer statuses. Do not convert blocked/not-run/inconclusive into PASS, represent an empty run as green, misclassify driver/infrastructure errors as product failures or erase an observed product failure after a later successful diagnostic attempt. All attempts and relevant prior failures remain inspectable; do not hide/mute them to obtain a favorable report.

If upstream charts exclude skipped/unknown outcomes or display the latest retry, retain a prominently available canonical summary/gap explanation alongside the view and within the retained report's linked evidence. The UI's run verdict and report-linked summary must not imply complete coverage from such a percentage. Report rendering does not itself prove execution or test success. Never import edits from rendered/exported artifacts back into canonical expectations/results.

**Acceptance.** A FAIL followed by PASS still yields the canonical FAILED result with the earlier violation visible. Passing cases plus a required blocked case remain INCOMPLETE in the workspace and report-linked summary even if an upstream chart looks green.
