The user can open a real Allure report and trace a displayed result to its exact canonical run/case revision without a custom replacement renderer.

### MT-033: Durable Report Generation And Recovery

**Behavior.** Preserve the separate Markdown report under MT-010 and retain the canonical run, sanitized Allure inputs, generated view and their provenance as distinguishable artifacts. Generate the required view from the identified saved run when reporting; expose generating/ready/failed/unavailable status rather than a ready link to absent or partial output. Use finite bounded, owned rendering work with MT-024-style admission for its actual execution host where material. A generation request/retry is identified and safe to reconcile; it does not repeat the SUT run or append fake observations.

A missing/incompatible renderer, timeout, nonzero outcome, absent expected artifacts, unsafe attachment or write failure leaves report delivery incomplete with the exact prerequisite and available saved results. A successful exit alone is not ready-view evidence. Preserve a product FAILED verdict and its additional delivery gaps rather than overwrite it with a renderer status. Provide the available summary/chat fallback without claiming a complete saved report. No automatic install/download or global setting change repairs a missing dependency. Regeneration uses retained canonical inputs/configuration and produces an identified artifact without overwriting prior reports or user edits.

Opening an already-ready report is view-only: it must not re-execute tests, rewrite case/result state, change workflow status or silently generate/migrate data. If generation is needed, show that state and an explicit safe retry/generation action. Preserve evidence for the saved report's usability; any retention/deletion change follows MT-025 and makes missing historical evidence explicit rather than reconstructing success.

**Acceptance.** An interrupted renderer leaves canonical observations and Markdown available, with no false ready-view link. Retrying generation produces a usable upstream view without another test execution or duplicate run. Reopening yesterday's report still resolves its original inputs and redacted attachments; unavailable evidence is visibly unavailable. A complete-testing response accounts for every relevant rendering/execution job and delivery prerequisite.

### MT-034: Minimal UI Journeys, Accessibility And Settings

**Behavior.** The first UI supports explicit project/library selection, bounded case/suite search/list/detail and revision-aware authoring, run list/detail and report/evidence opening, plus basic project/library/report configuration and dependency/version/readiness information. Settings do not add an account/team platform, arbitrary execution commands, a workflow designer or implicit migration/deletion. Basic configuration is validated before effect, preserves the previous valid configuration on failure and does not silently relocate historical data. Safe defaults do not change global host/client configuration.

For each relevant journey expose initial/no-project, loading, empty/no-match, selected/detail, invalid/unsaved, saving/pending, saved, stale/conflict, offline/unavailable, permission-denied and recoverable error states. Preserve input/selection where safe across failed operations; a project switch or cancellation does not silently save into another context. Show authoritative revision, run verdict and limitations using text, not color alone. Provide meaningful labels/roles, keyboard operation, logical focus, visible focus/error feedback and accessible status communication. Desktop resizing must keep primary actions/content usable; mobile support and exhaustive accessibility certification are not implied.

Use consistent interface text following repository localization while preserving user-authored Unicode case/oracle text and evidence without automatic translation. Exact visual design belongs to the separately invoked design stage and uses only the warranted shared components/variants and specification screens in the confirmed manifest, not a speculative full design system or a proprietary TestOps copy. No observed Penpot baseline is claimed by this specification.

**Acceptance.** A keyboard user can find/open/edit/save a case, observe validation and recover from a conflict without lost input or inaccessible feedback. An empty library differs visibly from a failed load. Resizing the desktop UI keeps the selected case/run and primary actions usable. A failed configuration change leaves prior valid behavior, and a run/report's incomplete status is understandable without interpreting a color or chart.

### MT-035: Coherent Public MCP And HTTP Contracts

**Behavior.** Expose compatible, discoverable testing operations for project/library access, bounded discovery/exact revision retrieval, definition mutations, frozen run/observation/checkpoint/finalization access and report state/generation/view access. UI HTTP operations and MCP capabilities share canonical identity, validation, authority, revision, ordering and failure semantics. Public success/error results distinguish invalid input, missing/foreign identity, denied authority, unsupported version/capability, stale revision/conflict, busy/unavailable, cancellation and uncertain/partial effects with bounded redacted guidance. No unknown operation or invalid input succeeds through a fallback.

Reads have no hidden mutation, migration or execution effect. Continuations bind the declared project/source/query/ref and preserve complete frozen enumeration under MT-020. Writes disclose acknowledgment/effects and retry identity; a lost response is not assumed not-applied. Checkpoints and multi-record changes cannot expose a mixed invalid state as successful. Cancellation/timeouts report actual known effects and preserve recoverable state, rather than roll back unknown effects by assertion. Required finite request/response/work limits are explicit in planning contracts; limit errors do not silently truncate canonical data or the selected denominator.

Publish observable contract/version compatibility and reject incompatible clients/data before effects. Do not silently drop unsupported fields, downgrade semantics or make standalone access depend on engineering-workflow MCP. Readiness/capability checks must not start scenarios or install components. Both skills use actual discovered host schemas without hard-coded generated namespaces; testing operations do not grant access to unrelated workflow decisions/task completion.

**Acceptance.** The same valid/invalid mutation through UI and MCP produces matching state/error semantics. An identical retry after a lost reply is inspectable/idempotent, while changed content with the same intent cannot silently execute twice. An old client cannot erase a newer required field. Pagination during unrelated observation appends terminates on its stated snapshot without an omitted final page or mixed-source data.

### MT-036: Local Access, Privacy And Untrusted Artifacts

**Behavior.** The first tool is single-user and local-only. Bind its UI/report service only to an explicitly local interface and deny unintended remote access; a displayed localhost URL is not proof of safe binding. Authorize browser/API/MCP access under the local operator's opened session/project scope, without introducing a team/account system. Protect state-changing and sensitive reads from unrelated web origins, forged/stale session context and local name/origin rebinding. A guessed project ID/path or encoded context alone is not authority. Failure to establish the required access boundary fails closed without leaking data in errors/logs.

Restrict operations to explicitly authorized managed library/report areas. Reject unsafe traversal, foreign-project references, links/aliases or attachment names that escape those boundaries; never serve arbitrary process-readable files or execute data/configuration as code. Reports, imported metadata, target text and attachments are untrusted data. Isolate or safely refuse active HTML/script content so viewing evidence cannot inherit access to tool credentials, other projects or mutation endpoints; retain a safe unavailable/download explanation where a dangerous inline view is refused. Do not weaken these controls merely to make an upstream report server work.

Apply MT-007 redaction before storage/export, including renderer inputs, hidden/masked values, logs/screenshots and attachments; hiding a value in UI is not deletion from an artifact. Do not persist access/session secrets in public links, manifests, reports or diagnostics. Use least-privilege local storage/access and invalidate obsolete session context on restart/authority change. The contract does not claim protection against an arbitrary malicious process already holding the operator's same OS privileges, but that limit cannot excuse an exposed browser/remote endpoint.

**Acceptance.** An unrelated origin, forged project context or escaping attachment path receives a safe denial with no protected bytes, mutation or command execution. A report with hostile active content cannot invoke tool operations or read another project's data. Actual listener/access observations establish local-only behavior, and retained evidence contains no credentials or unrelated private paths.

### MT-037: Standalone Local Lifecycle And Owned Recovery

**Behavior.** Support explicit local startup/shutdown and UI/report use without an active AI agent or MCP client. Show the actual ready endpoint/project context and dependency/version state; an occupied port, wrong service, incompatible data or startup failure ends within a finite bound and does not kill an unrelated process, relabel another endpoint as this tool or auto-install/configure anything. Preserve declared Linux/Windows/macOS behavior while reporting only MT-028's actual development evidence.

Data survives ordinary close/restart and remains identifiable independently of a chat. Cooperating UI/MCP sessions may access the same owned library without silent lost updates; a conflicting instance/operation is serialized safely or reported busy/conflicting rather than corrupting state. Closing one client must not terminate unrelated clients' resources or a healthy owned test batch merely to finish a chat turn. Track ownership of service/rendering processes, temporary files and access/session handles; stop/release only verified owned resources, preserving retained evidence and pre-existing services.

On interruption, reconcile persisted run/operation receipts and actual resource state under MT-012/MT-025 before continuation. Never infer completion from a stale UI cache, a dead connection or an old process ID. Explicit repair/restore requires established authority and preserves a known valid prior state, identities and run references; do not steal unknown locks by age, silently migrate data or replay non-idempotent tests. Uncertain live resources or failed cleanup remain visible with the exact next action. Rendering has owned bounded lifecycle; the tool does not take over native test execution or stand provisioning.

**Acceptance.** After the agent exits, the operator can explicitly launch the UI and inspect saved cases/runs/reports without rerunning tests. Restart after an interrupted save yields validated prior/new state or an explicit recovery prerequisite, never false saved success. Port collision and cancellation leave unrelated processes untouched. Losing one client does not silently destroy another client's session or treat unknown jobs as collected.

## Non-Goals

Native background execution, relevant safety/accessibility and the selected local testing-runtime MCP/HTTP/UI/Allure integration remain in scope. Penpot editing and all profile/design artifact creation belong to later separately invoked stages, not this specification invocation. Future implementation is deferred, not cancelled.
